I've saved the answers to `/work/answer.json`. I checked them a second way with plain SQL and both methods gave the same numbers.

```json
{"a_segment": "enterprise", "a_net": 333415095, "b_customers": 248, "c_category": "svc", "c_net": 335927781, "d_month": "2025-07", "e_email": "u158@ex.com", "f_repeat": 239, "g_avg": 693045, "h_growth": 3.4}
```

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with highest Q3 net sales | enterprise, 333,415,095원 (smb 306,882,752 / consumer 231,553,898) |
| b. Customers with a paid Q3 order | 248 (by email) |
| c. Category with highest Q3 net sales | svc, 335,927,781원 |
| d. Month with highest net sales overall | 2025-07 (296,788,093원) |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refund total | u158@ex.com (2,679,900원, no tie) |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid Q3 orders | 239 |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 693,045원 (871,851,745원 ÷ 1,258 orders) |
| h. Sep vs Aug growth | 3.4% (282,743,834 → 292,319,818원, raw 3.387%) |

**How I handled the data:**
- Segment values had stray spaces and mixed case (`' consumer'`, `'Enterprise '`, `'SMB'`, …). After trimming and lowercasing they collapse into 3 segments.
- There are 300 accounts but only 250 distinct emails, so b, e and f count by email. By account, b would be 295.
- All timestamps were shifted +9 hours (KST) before assigning dates, so an order at `2025-06-30T22:31Z` counts as July and one at `2025-09-30T14:30Z` counts as October.
- Refunds have no timestamp of their own, so each refund counts in the month of its original order. All refunds are on paid orders.
- Only status `paid` (2,382 orders) is counted; cancelled and pending orders are left out.

**Judgment call in a:** 32 emails have accounts in different segments. I took the segment from the account that placed each order. If you instead give each person one segment (taken from their lowest-numbered account), the amounts change (enterprise 314,150,679원), but enterprise is still first.
